concepts.def: Repeated cycle of designing, prototyping and testing that progressively refines a product based on feedback.
Initial statement of the problem and requirements set by a client or identified through research, initiating the design process.
Set of measurable criteria a product must meet, covering function, materials, dimensions, cost and user needs.
Working or appearance model of a design used to test ideas, gather user feedback and refine specifications.
Critical review of a prototype against the specification, identifying improvements for the next iteration.
Information gathered from intended users through interviews, observation or testing, feeding decisions for iteration.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Current Legislation — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Current Legislation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Current Legislation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which document sets out measurable criteria a product must meet?
options: Brief
Specification
Catalogue
Bill of materials
Single linear process
Repeated cycles of refinement
No prototyping
Fixed first solution

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: They are the same thing with different names.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
Current stays the same.

mcqs.q: If voltage is doubled and resistance is unchanged, what happens to the current?
options: Current stays the same.
Current halves.
Current doubles (V = IR, so I = V/R).
Thinking about marketing the product.

mcqs.q: What does 'Rethink' mean in the 6 Rs?
options: Thinking about marketing the product.
Trying a design again if it does not work first time.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Questioning whether a product is necessary or could be designed differently for sustainability.
